articles.title: Arise, Sir Harry? Downing Street hints at Kane knighthood after Ballon d’Or win
articles.summary: Andy Burnham sends congratulations to England captain. Bayern player is first Englishman to win award since 2001. Downing Street has hinted that Harry Kane deserves a knighthood, praising the footballer’s “extraordinary achievement” as the first English winner of the Ballon d’Or in 25 years.
body: The prime minister’s spokesperson said Andy Burnham sent praise and congratulations to the England captain, who was announced as the men’s winner of football’s most prestigious individual award at a ceremony on Monday night.

Number 10 said it hoped it would be the prelude to a trophy to celebrate with England “before too long” – alluding to hopes of an England win when the country co-hosts the European Championship in 2028 with Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The Bayern Munich player is the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. “The PM would like to congratulate Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d’Or,” the spokesperson said. “To be the first Englishman to win it in 25 years is an extraordinary achievement, and what a moment to do it here at home.

“Seventy years after Sir Stanley Matthews won the inaugural award, it caps a remarkable season and Harry continues to set a brilliant example to young players across the country, and the PM knows the whole nation will be incredibly proud of him. And, hopefully, there’s another trophy to celebrate with England before too long.”

articles.title: Alexia Putellas a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but the limited shortlist illustrates flaws
articles.summary: Neglect of African football and a third win for the Spanish great does little to challenge narrative that the prize is reserved only for top nations’ players. After a four-year wait, Alexia Putellas is the queen of women’s football once again.
body: It was the sixth consecutive year in which the honour went to either Putellas or her international teammate, Aitana Bonmatí, and it was symbolic of Putellas’ resurgence after her comeback from the anterior cruciate ligament injury she suffered in her left knee in 2022, her refusal to surrender her career to that setback, and her majestic rise back to the top.

The midfielder’s competition-leading 14 goal contributions – eight goals and six assists – in 11 Women’s Champions League appearances last season, helping Barcelona lift the European title, went a long way to her securing the most votes, as well as her starring role in Spain’s victory in the Women’s Nations League finals last December. Her new club, London City Lionesses, will rejoice in the prestige of having the Ballon d’Or winner in their squad but Putellas, who spent 14 yeas at Barcelona, made it clear whom she wanted to thank as she said in her acceptance speech “This prize is for Barcelona.”

articles.title: Wolff rejects Marko's doubts over Russell's future F1 title hopes
articles.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff has rejected Helmut Marko's suggestion that George Russell has little chance of becoming Formula 1 world champion in the future after being outperformed by his team-mate Kimi Antonelli this season.
body: Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix on Sunday to move to the brink of being crowed the sport's youngest ever champion, with the 20-year-old only needing to finish ninth this weekend in the Mexico City Grand Prix to seal the title with four rounds to spare.

Perhaps the most shocking element of the Italian's historic campaign has been the way he has outperformed Russell, who had begun the season as the clear title favourite after dominating Antonelli during the latter's rookie season last year.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's race in Austin, former Red Bull motorsport advisor Marko told Sky Germany: "Mentally, it's certainly a massive setback and it's a blow. Russell is no longer the number one driver."

"Antonelli has quite clearly taken that spot from him. But Russell is one of the top drivers. I doubt whether he'll ever have another chance at the world title or be given number one status anywhere."

articles.title: Pierre Sage given more time by Crystal Palace but remains under pressure
articles.summary: Frenchman’s future was in doubt after bad start to season. He could be sacked if Palace lose at Spurs on Saturday. Pierre Sage has been given more time to turn around Crystal Palace’s fortunes but he remains under huge pressure and could be dismissed if they lose against Tottenham on Saturday.
body: The Frenchman’s position was in serious doubt after another poor performance in the 2-0 defeat against Newcastle at the weekend. That followed a 5-0 thrashing against Brighton when Sage was warned that he could be dismissed if results did not improve quickly.

However the club’s chair, Steve Parish, has decided not to act given the tight turnaround in Palace’s schedule: the side face Fulham at Craven Cottage in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, before their trip to Tottenham in the Premier League. But Sage, who attended the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on Monday evening, is understood to have been left in no doubt that the meeting with Spurs on Saturday is crucial to his future.

Palace are 17th and have conceded 19 goals in eight Premier League matchesthis season – the highest in the division. But, it is understood, Sage retains the support of his squad, with two leading players having sent him messages saying that they still have faith he can turn things around.

articles.title: Carrick given chance to save job as he stays for Manchester United’s game at Chelsea
articles.summary: Jason Wilcox has driven decision to stand by head coach. United would have to pay Newcastle about £3m for Howe. Michael Carrick has been given the chance to save his job by turning Manchester United’s results around, with the head coach remaining in place for Saturday’s visit to Chelsea.
body: The decision by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, can be viewed as a surprise given United’s dire form.
Sunday’s abject 3-0 league home defeat by Bournemouth followed Wednesday’s equally poor 4-1 reverse at Como in the Champions League.
Carrick’s side have won twice in 12 games and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Brighton. United are 16th in the Premier League, a point above the relegation zone.

Yet Wilcox, who has driven the retaining of Carrick, wants to give the 45-year-old a chance to transform form and results. Whether Carrick could survive another poor performance and result at Stamford Bridge is in the balance.

articles.title: Osaka's outfit dazzles again in Japan win as Williams loses to teenager
articles.summary: Home favourite Naomi Osaka said she wanted to bring "a bit of a show" to the Pan Pacific Open after wearing a Japan-inspired outfit before beating Italy's Jasmine Paolini in the opening round.
body: The seventh seed defeat Paolini in 6-3 7-6 (4) in a match lasting one hour and 37 minutes in Tokyo, saving saved three consecutive set points in the second set before sealing victory in the tiebreak to advance to the second round.

Osaka returned to Tokyo for the first time in four years and wore a blue-and-white, crane-embroidered kimono-inspired outfit designed by Hana Yagi - who created her Wimbledon outfit - as she entered the WTA 500 event.

"I was just really glad that she [Yagi] wanted to work with me again," Osaka said. "I feel like for me I haven't been here in a little bit of a while, so It's just nice to bring a bit of a show here too."

Victory for Osaka avenges her loss to Paolini last year in the Miami Open, their only previous meeting, with the 29-year-old racking up seven aces to her opponent's one during the tournament-opening victory.

articles.title: McInnes admits 'guilt' over Hearts exit for Rangers
articles.summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes admits feeling "guilt" about leaving Hearts for Ibrox in the summer and accepts the rough reception that could come his way when he returns to Tynecastle on Wednesday.
body: After coming within minutes of Hearts' first top-flight title in 66 years, only to lose out to Celtic on the last day, McInnes says he is proud of what he achieved at the "really well-run" Edinburgh club.
And he believes Hearts are "absolutely title contenders" this term under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.
But he is not expecting a warm welcome, despite handing over a squad that came so close to breaking the dominance of Celtic and his current club.
"Well, the hope would be that you get on to the pitch and clap the fans and there's an acknowledgement both ways, but that's not going to happen," McInnes said.

articles.title: Simpler, cheaper hybrid V8s proposed for next F1 rules
articles.summary: Formula 1's next engine regulations are set to introduce V8 turbo hybrid engines that are simplified and less expensive compared to the existing rules.
body: A proposal document sent by governing body the FIA to the six manufacturers in F1 outlines a framework for discussions on engines to be introduced in either 2030 or 2031.
Multiple sources within F1 have provided BBC Sport with the details within the document.
The plan, which comes after initial discussions with individual engine manufacturers on a one-to-one basis, proposes cheaper, lighter, simpler engines with a more visceral sound.
However, the FIA has moved away from its initial proposal to return to naturally aspirated engines.

articles.title: How Kane's Ballon d'Or win could boost the Bundesliga
articles.summary: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win not only ended a 25-year wait for an English winner of the award but also saw a Bundesliga player win it for the first time since 1996.
body: England has had to wait a long time for another winner of the Ballon d'Or, with Harry Kane on Monday night becoming the first player from the country to win it for 25 years.
But his success has also been celebrated in Germany with the Bayern Munich striker ending their even longer run without a player from the Bundesliga lifting the coveted trophy.
The last to do so was Matthias Sammer back in 1996 after he had captained Borussia Dortmund to two successive Bundesliga titles.
"Just as Bayern and the Bundesliga benefit from Kane, the reverse is also true," Lothar Matthaus, the most capped German player of all time and 1991 Ballon d'Or winner, said.

articles.title: Brewers star Jackson Chourio joins Ty Cobb in World Series history
articles.summary: MLB history was made Monday night as Milwaukee Brewers star Jackson Chourio delivered a remarkable performance, joining legendary Hall of Famer Ty Cobb in an exclusive World Series record during the team’s dominant 10-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 3.
body: At 22 years and 229 days old, Chourio became the youngest player since Cobb in 1908 to record four hits and a stolen base in a World Series game. Cobb was just 21 when he accomplished the feat more than a century ago, placing Chourio among some of baseball’s most memorable postseason performers.
The young outfielder went four-for-five at the plate, helping Milwaukee move within one win of its first championship in franchise history.
“I was ready,” Chourio said after the game through an interpreter. “I was ready, and I wanted to win today.”

Chourio has been one of Milwaukee’s biggest offensive contributors throughout the World Series. Through the first three games, he has recorded eight hits, scored four runs, stolen three bases and driven in two runs.
